answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove duplicate behavior, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs real capital. Like a knoll that only rises above the flood after sustained work, reputation must accrue slowly from verified transactions, while a wharf charges a docking fee per identity, making mass onboarding expensive. A public mirror of stakes and history lets anyone audit who is real.
